_comment: CANONICAL test-composition target for EVERY generated test in EVERY course of Physics Academy. Referenced by build/render/unit-test.js (assembly-time pool check) and js/unit-test.js (attempt-time stratified sampling). It is also the authoring target for the question banks: a unit's bank should hold enough items in each difficulty and cognitive band to let a 45-minute test be drawn to this distribution. Rationale, sources, and how-to in docs/test-generation.md. Change this file only with a matching docs update and a version bump.

pointSplit._comment: Share of TOTAL TEST POINTS from each section, not item count. An MCQ is worth 1 point; an FRQ is worth its totalPoints. AP Physics 1 (2025) weights the multiple-choice and free-response sections exactly 50/50; IB Physics (2025 syllabus) leans more to constructed response, but a 50/50 practice split builds both the fast-recognition and the extended-reasoning skills a 90%+ student needs.

difficultyDistribution._comment: Target share of ITEMS at each taxonomies.json difficulty level. Deliberately HARDER than a live exam (which, mapped to this scale, runs roughly 15/25/35/20/5). The median practice item is 'ap-ib-standard' and 35% sit AT OR ABOVE the AP-5 / IB-7 line, so a student who comfortably clears our tests is well past the ~70% composite that earns a 5 or a 7 and is on track for 90%+. See docs/test-generation.md 'Why train above the exam'.

cognitiveDistribution._comment: Target share of items per cognitive band. Bands group the 8-level cognitiveLevel scale in rigor-standard-addendum.md section 2. AP Physics 1 and IB Physics are reasoning-first exams (the CED science practices and the IB assessment objectives are dominated by application, analysis and evaluation), so band C is intentionally large.

timing._comment: Per-item minute estimates for time-budget mode (config.mode == 'time'). MCQ figure is the AP Physics 1 2025 rate (80 min / 40 questions). FRQ figure is scaled down from the AP rate (100 min / 4 fifteen-point questions ~ 1.6 min/pt) because our lesson-style FRQs are shorter and lower-stakes.

calculatorPolicyByCourse._comment: Default calculator policy for the MCQ section of a generated test, by course. When 'not-allowed', js/unit-test.js shows a no-calculator banner AND the assembler draws the MCQ pool only from items flagged calculatorFree:true. NOTE: the CURRENT IB Physics syllabus (first exams 2025) PERMITS a calculator on Paper 1A; the pre-2025 Paper 1 did not. The default below follows the project owner's directive that DP MCQ practice be doable without a calculator; flip to 'allowed' to match the 2025 syllabus. A per-test `calculatorPolicy` in the content file overrides this.

unitTest._comment: Every unit in every course gets exactly one of these, delivered as a `format: "unit-test"` page.

toleranceOnDistribution._comment: How far the attempt-time draw may fall from the target shares before js/unit-test.js stops trying to match and just fills from the remaining pool. Also the slack the assembler's pool-adequacy warning allows.
